title: Service Layer

validation.research: Six primary-source notes. Randy Stafford’s Service Layer entry in Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture establishes the application boundary, operations, coordination, and transaction responsibility. Percival and Gregory demonstrate interface-independent orchestration and distinguish application services from domain services. Fowler supports the separate choice of Transaction Script and the anemic-model caution. Official Python and SQLite documentation support the explicit local transaction mechanism. Workshop code and native diagrams are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: All three actual article fences execute as model.py, application.py, and demo.py, producing five stated lines exactly. Checks cover positive whole-seat requests, nonnegative availability, exact final-seat booking, immutable model snapshots, duplicate primary-key failure after the capacity update with complete rollback, unknown workshops, invalid inputs, opaque IDs including quotes and surrounding spaces, rejection of non-explicit or nested transactions without altering caller work, caller-owned connection lifetime, trace ordering, two-connection write contention, and committed cross-connection visibility. BEGIN IMMEDIATE lock failure produces no successful booking. The duplicate attempt restores capacity and allows the other caller to take the final seat.

example_limits: Python 3.10+ with standard-library SQLite. The caller supplies an idle connection configured for explicit SQL transaction control and owns closing it. The original local operation demonstrates capacity validation, two writes, commit, and rollback. The in-memory demo has no web server or CLI parser; its labels represent two callers. It implements no authentication, notifications, waitlist, cancellation, durable retry/idempotency outcome protocol, distributed transaction, or automatic contention retry. Duplicate booking IDs are rejected rather than returning an earlier outcome. Remaining seats describe the result immediately after this operation, not future availability. SQLite’s write transaction supplies the shown concurrency protection; a Service Layer name does not create it.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
